It is characterized by the sudden loss of function of the proximal tubules and interstitium. The pathogenesis of ATN is multifactorial and includes ischemia, hypoxia, inflammation, and direct toxic effects of the nephrotoxic agent. The clinical presentation of ATN is usually abrupt onset of oliguria, hyperkalemia, metabolic acidosis, and azotemia. The kidneys are enlarged and have a mottled appearance on imaging studies. Histologically, there is loss of tubular epithelial cells, interstitial edema, and hemorrhage.
